outcome: Length of labor and delivery stay
cohort: 331 women undergoing induction of labor at 37-41 weeks gestation with a Bishop score ≤4
finding: Single-dose misoprostol was more efficient for induction of labor at term, resulting in decreased time to active labor, time to delivery, and length of labor and delivery stay, without increasing adverse obstetrical outcomes, and was associated with cost savings compared to dinoprostone.
mod_finding: Single-dose misoprostol was found to be more efficient than dinoprostone for induction of labor at term, leading to decreased time to active labor, time to delivery, and length of labor and delivery stay, without increasing adverse outcomes.
